Chapter 8: The Law of Financial Viability — Ensuring Your Mission is Sustainable.
Chasing a mission that matters to you is incredibly rewarding. But here’s the thing—if you want that mission to last, it needs to be sustainable, too. The law of financial viability is a reminder that meaningful work has to support your life, not just your ideals.
Now, this isn't about putting money above everything else. It’s about making sure your mission can actually keep going and even grow. Think about an artist who loves painting community murals. Their work lights up neighborhoods and inspires people. But if it doesn’t pay the bills or fund future projects, how long can they really keep it up?
So, what can that artist do? Maybe they start offering workshops, selling prints, or applying for grants. By finding ways to turn their passion into income, they’re building a solid base for their creative work to continue—and thrive.
When you apply the law of financial viability, you’re really asking a few key questions. Can this mission or project actually support your financial needs? Are there different ways to earn income that still fit your values? And are you open to making changes if one approach just isn’t working out?
Here’s something to notice—taking care of your financial health doesn’t limit your creativity. If anything, it gives you more freedom and a bigger impact. Financial stability lets you focus on what matters, experiment, and reach more people.
So, think of this principle not as a restriction, but as a safety net. It’s there to make sure your search for meaning doesn’t put your well-being or your future at risk. When you weave financial viability into your mission, you’re setting yourself up for lasting fulfillment and the ability to make a real difference—year after year.
